history_note: T0030 and T0031 are PRESERVED unchanged. This receipt records a further correction found inside the same authorization; migration 0012 is corrected ADDITIVELY by 0013 rather than rewritten.

findings_absorbed.what_was_true: T0031 made every Engine and DarkGuard field unexported, which closed the MUTATION hole. It did not close the CONSTRUCTION hole: NewEngine remained exported and accepted a caller-supplied Config and a caller-supplied Transport, so production code could still have built an independently configured, independently transported financial sender in one struct literal.
findings_absorbed.correction: NewProductionEngine(repo, getenv) is now the ONLY exported constructor and takes neither. Config comes from the fail-closed environment loader; the transport comes from an internal factory which in this build returns nothing, and which REFUSES TO START if transmission is enabled against a build with no transport. The deterministic test seam moved to export_test.go, which the Go toolchain compiles only for this package's own tests, so a production binary does not contain it. The DARK CI check asserts the wrap, the absence of exported fields, the constructor signature, the absence of any other exported constructor taking a Transport, and the presence of the compile-time-only seam.

findings_absorbed.what_was_true: Migration 0012 read 'programmatic reversal is capability=false' and refused REVERSAL posting rows outright. That over-constrained the contract and made a required workflow unimplementable. The FINAL Phase-0 Contract states BOTH halves: section 9a rule 5 and Gate 3B make the EXECUTABLE reversal unsupported in v1 with PT=C and negative TA unverified and never transmissible; sections 15 and 16 require CREATE_REVERSAL to produce 'a new ledger row referencing the original' and state that 'reversal is a new REVERSAL row'. 0012 forbade the row as well as the sender, which would also have removed the audited record that Gate 3B requires in exchange for deferring the capability.
findings_absorbed.correction: Migration 0013 separates them. The passive ledger row is permitted and is written ONLY by the audited CREATE_REVERSAL review action, referencing an in-scope original CHARGE, in the same currency and exponent, with a POSITIVE amount (direction is carried by posting_type, never by a negative TA), bounded so cumulative reversals can never exceed the charge. The row is structurally inert: p4_reversal_never_queued and p4_reversal_never_attempted make it impossible for it to acquire an outbox row or an attempt, so it can never allocate a P# or produce a byte. No executable reversal sender exists, no PT=C appears anywhere, and no negative TA is ever stored. The transmission-protecting gates (freshness, lifecycle, FIAS exponent) are correctly not applied to a record that never transmits, so a correction can still be recorded while the interface is down -- which is when corrections happen.
